headline: GOLD BREAKS BELOW $4,000 AS FED RATE HIKE ODDS HIT 90% — SPOT FALLS $147 TO $3,891 IN BIGGEST SINGLE-DAY DROP IN WEEKS
snippet: Gold spot fell to $3,890 on Thursday, November 12, losing more than $140 from Wednesday's close as Federal Reserve rate-hike odds for the December 8-9 meeting crystallize at roughly 90%. The dollar strengthened sharply on the expectation of a 25-basis-point hike, erasing gold's post-midterm rebound and pushing silver below $51 in tandem.

headline: MAMMOTH MINERALS (ASX:M79) HALTED AHEAD OF TRIPLE DEAL — CAPITAL RAISE, ACQUISITION AND OFFTAKE BEFORE NOV. 16 OPEN
snippet: Mammoth Minerals Limited (ASX:M79), which holds the Excelsior Springs gold-silver project in Nevada, requested an ASX trading halt on November 12 pending a simultaneous announcement covering a material capital raising, a potential acquisition, and an offtake agreement. The halt is expected to run until November 16; details of the acquisition target and offtake counterparty have not yet been disclosed.

headline: INDIA BANS LITHIUM BATTERY BLACK MASS EXPORTS — DOMESTIC PROCESSING PUSH RESHAPES BATTERY SUPPLY CHAIN
snippet: India prohibited exports of lithium-ion battery black mass on November 11, banning the outflow of recycled EV battery material that contains lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese. The policy forces domestic processing of end-of-life batteries, adding India to a growing list of countries prioritizing battery material sovereignty — and signalling that the EV supply chain is increasingly fragmented by jurisdiction.

headline: SILVER HITS 1-YEAR LOW — GOLD ALSO FALLS AS PRECIOUS METALS ENTER CORRECTION AHEAD OF DEC FED MEETING
snippet: Silver fell to its lowest level in a year on Tuesday, November 10, pulling gold lower alongside it as dollar strength tied to December Fed rate-hike expectations undermines both metals. The move tests the thesis that silver's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit provides fundamental price support — a thesis that now faces its sharpest challenge since the summer.

headline: COPPER FALLS TO 4-MONTH LOW AT $6.20/LB — PAPER MARKET CRACKS DESPITE RECORD $230 YANGSHAN PHYSICAL PREMIUM
snippet: LME copper slid 1.18% to $6.20 per pound on November 12, its lowest level since July, despite the Yangshan import premium — a gauge of real demand in China — hitting a record $230 per tonne. The divergence between weakening paper prices and persistently tight physical markets signals that macro concerns about a potential U.S. rate hike are overriding near-term supply constraints.

headline: USA RARE EARTH JUMPS 11% ONE DAY AFTER Q3 MISS — MP MATERIALS CLIMBS 4% AS RARE EARTH SECTOR STABILIZES
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) staged an 11% recovery on November 11, one session after shares cratered following a Q3 revenue miss. MP Materials climbed 4% in the same session. China's two-month extension of rare earth export-control waivers, announced November 9, removed the near-term binary risk and provided a floor for the sector after the volatile earnings week.

headline: UR-ENERGY Q3: $12.3M REVENUE MISSES CONSENSUS BUT YTD URANIUM SALES UP 67% — SHIRLEY BASIN DELIVERS FIRST POUNDS
snippet: Ur-Energy (NYSE American: URG) reported Q3 2026 product revenue of $12.3 million on 190,000 pounds sold, below the analyst consensus of $14.87 million, with an EPS loss of $0.06. Despite the quarterly miss, year-to-date uranium sales volumes are up 67.3% over 2025 and the company made its first deliveries of uranium captured at Shirley Basin — marking a production diversification milestone as the two-mine platform ramps.

headline: CITI SLASHES LITHIUM FORECASTS 40% FOR 2027-2028 — SURPLUS THROUGH 2028, ALBEMARLE AND SQM FACE PROLONGED PRESSURE
snippet: Citigroup cut its two-year lithium price forecasts by as much as 40%, citing slower battery demand growth, rising Chinese production and increased trade uncertainty. The bank expects the market to remain in surplus through 2028. The revised outlook adds institutional weight to a bearish consensus that has already pushed Chinese lithium carbonate down roughly 21% since early November.

headline: UZBEKISTAN TARGETS 15,000 TONNES URANIUM BY 2030 — DOUBLES CURRENT OUTPUT, ADDS NON-KAZAKH SUPPLY TO GLOBAL MARKET
snippet: Uzbekistan plans to double its uranium production from approximately 7,500 tonnes currently to 15,000 tonnes by 2030, according to World Nuclear News. The expansion adds a meaningful new source of non-Russian, non-Kazakh supply to the global market at a time when Western utilities are actively diversifying uranium procurement — but it also represents structural long-term headwind for spot prices if demand growth disappoints.

headline: STRONG COPPER PRICES DRIVE RECORD Q3 EARNINGS FOR MAJOR MINERS — NEW CAPACITY PLANS SIGNAL SUPPLY SURGE AHEAD
snippet: Major copper producers reported strong to record third-quarter earnings on November 12, lifted by prices that remain roughly 23% above year-ago levels despite recent weakness. Alongside the strong results, multiple producers announced new capacity expansion plans that analysts say could add significant supply by the late 2020s — a potential headwind for the junior exploration companies that retail investors typically hold.

headline: WHY GOLD MINERS ROSE ON GOLD'S DOWN DAY — EARLY STRENGTH SIGNAL OR FALSE DAWN FOR JUNIOR MINING STOCKS?
snippet: Analyst Przemyslaw Radomski examines the unusual session on November 9 when junior gold miners outperformed physical gold on a down day — a pattern historically associated with sector bottoming behavior. He cautions that the broader stock market's next directional move will likely determine whether miners confirm a reversal or resume their steep underperformance relative to gold bullion near $4,000.
